newsitem.title: UK: UK electric industry too crowded - PowerGen.
newsitem.headline: UK electric industry too crowded - PowerGen.

text.p: PowerGen chairman Ed Wallis on Wednesday attacked Britain's Office of Electricity Regulation (Offer) for promoting an industry crowded with firms which he said lack the ability to survive as effective competitors.
"This idea, which seems to have been promulgated by Offer, that..the ideal generation market is one that is atomised, is a very dangerous one," he told Parliament's Trade and Industry Committee.

Wallis said the plant of many of the new entrants to the market, who had come in on the back of long-term contracts with the regional electricity companies, had been "not as reliable as one would have expected".

"I am not sure that is really the best way of introducing competition because these players do not have the skills and the throw-weight...to survive as effective players in the market in the longer term," he added. Wallis said the most effective and competitive market would be a vertically integrated one, in which there were five or six players "with real critical mass in there for the long term with the critical core skills to invest and run effective plant."
But other industry companies suggested to the committee that more participants should be welcomed into the generation market.

"So that consumers can receive the full benefit of competition, government policy should strongly encourage more participants to enter the electricity generation market," Gale Klappa, chief executive of South Western Electricity Plc, said in a written submission.
